entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:1
segments:
In this chapter the heavenly Solomon sets forth the beauty and majesty of his bride. 
 
  As a flock of goats; the comparison respects the hair. 
 
  Gilead; a region east of the Jordan, celebrated for the excellence of its pasture-grounds.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:2
segments: Like a flock of sheep; in whiteness.  What follows is added to show their soundness and vigor.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:4
segments: Like the tower of David; for strength and majesty.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:6
segments: Until the day break; see note on
.  From the mountains of myrrh and the hill of frankincense he gathers perfumes for his love, that she may be "perfumed with myrrh and frankincense."

entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:7
segments: The heavenly bride, the Lamb's wife, is "the perfection of beauty, the joy of the whole earth."  She embraces in herself all the true excellence that is found among men.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:8
segments:
Here begins a new representation, in which, for the first time, the bride is addressed by the title of "spouse." 
 
  Come with me from Lebanon; these words seem to be spoken on the top of Lebanon, where Solomon, who represents the heavenly Bridegroom, has been showing his bride the glory of his kingdom.  He calls her to take a like survey of it from the top of Amana and Hermon.
The ridge of Hermon lies east of Lebanon.  It was called Shenir by the Amorites.

Amana was probably a peak of the same range, from which the river of the same name flowed. 
 
  From the lions' dens; that is, from the tops of the mountains, that abound in lions' dens.  In showing his bride these goodly possessions, the king gives her a pledge that she shall share with him dominion over them.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:12
segments: Inclosed--shut up--sealed; guarded from intrusion, and reserved for the king's enjoyment. For the spiritual meaning, compare

. 
 
Christ will not share with others the affections of his people.  If they would have him dwell in their garden, its fruits must be consecrated to him alone.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:15
segments:
A fountain of gardens; lying among gardens and watering them. 
 
  Streams from Lebanon; cool and refreshing.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 4:16
segments: Awake, O north wind; the wind is a symbol of the quickening and life-giving power of the Holy Spirit.

, the spouse was herself a garden, and its precious fruits her graces.  Here she has charge of a garden.  The meaning is the same. 
 
The fruitfulness of God's people depends upon the presence and life-giving power of the Holy Spirit, by whom alone they can be made meet for communion with their Redeemer.
